words.ex: We achieved our export target this quarter.
use: She achieved great results in the new market.
그녀는 새 시장에서 좋은 성과를 냈다.
What do you want to achieve this year?
mcq: He achieved to increase sales.
He achieved a 20% increase in sales.
He achieved in the sales target.
He was achieved the target.
words.note: achieve + 명사(목표·성과). achieve to는 쓰지 않아요.

words.ex: I built my career in overseas sales.
use: This project was a turning point in my career.
She started her career as an intern.
mcq: My career is a salesperson.
I've spent my career in cosmetics.
I am career in sales.
My career works in sales field.
words.note: career는 직업명이 아니라 '경력의 흐름'. My job is~ 와 구분!

words.ex: Our goal is to enter the US market.
use: We set clear goals for each quarter.
The team reached its sales goal early.
mcq: We set a goal for next year.
We made a goal for next year.
We built a goal for next year.
We put a goal to next year.
words.note: set a goal이 정확한 짝(collocation)이에요.

words.ex: Feel free to contact me anytime.
use: I'll contact the buyer this week.
mcq: Please contact to me by email.
Please contact with me by email.
Please contact me by email.
Please contact for me by email.
words.note: contact + 사람 바로! contact to/with는 한국식 오류의 대표주자.

words.ex: I regard him as a mentor.
use: She is regarded as an expert in K-beauty.
Please give my regards to your team.
mcq: I regard him as a good partner.
I regard him a good partner.
I regard him to a good partner.
I regard him being good partner.
words.note: regard A as B. as를 빼먹기 쉬워요! 이메일 끝 Best regards도 이 단어.

words.ex: I have 10 years of experience in sales.
use: We experienced some delays in shipping.
mcq: I have many experiences of sales.
I have a lot of experience in sales.
I have much experience about sales.
I am experienced of sales.
words.note: 경력의 experience는 셀 수 없는 명사! experience in + 분야.

words.ex: Please inform us of any changes.
use: I'll inform the client about the delay.
We were informed that the meeting was canceled.
mcq: I informed the schedule to him.
I informed him of the schedule.
I informed to him the schedule.
I informed about him the schedule.
words.note: inform + 사람 + of/about + 내용. 사람이 먼저 와요!

words.ex: Let's examine the contract carefully.
use: The team examined the market data.
mcq: We examined the samples closely.
We examined about the samples.
We examined on the samples.
We made examine the samples.
words.note: examine + 대상 바로 연결. review보다 더 꼼꼼히 보는 느낌이에요.

words.ex: We received some negative feedback.
use: Don't be so negative about the plan.
mcq: The feedback was negative.
The feedback was negatively.
The feedback did negative.
The feedback was in negative.
words.note: be + negative(형용사). 검사 결과 '음성'도 negative예요.

words.ex: They're our biggest business partner.
use: We partnered with a local distributor.
Finding the right partner takes time.
맞는 파트너를 찾는 데는 시간이 걸린다.
mcq: We partnered with a Chinese company.
We partnered to a Chinese company.
We made partner a company.
We partnered a company together with.
words.note: partner with + 회사 = ~와 제휴하다. 동사로도 써요!

words.ex: What's the procedure for customs clearance?
use: The visa procedure takes two weeks.
mcq: Follow the safety procedure.
Follow the safety proceed.
Follow the safety procession.
Follow the safety process of procedure.
words.note: procedure(절차) vs process(과정) vs proceed(진행하다) — 셋을 구분!

words.ex: We conducted a customer survey.
use: The company conducts market research every year.
The interview was conducted in English.
mcq: We conducted a meeting with the buyer.
We conducted to a meeting.
We were conduct a meeting.
We conducted for a meeting.
words.note: conduct + 조사/회의/실험. do보다 격식 있는 비즈니스 동사!

words.ex: Speak with confidence in the meeting.
use: I have confidence in our product.
The buyer lost confidence in the supplier.
바이어가 그 공급사에 대한 신뢰를 잃었다.
mcq: I have confidence in this plan.
I have confidence to this plan.
I have confidence about this plan well.
I am confidence in this plan.
words.note: confidence in + 대상. 형용사는 confident (I am confident)!

words.ex: You need a permit to sell here.
use: The law doesn't permit this kind of ad.
Weather permitting, we'll visit the factory.
mcq: Smoking is not permitted here.
Smoking is not permitting here.
Smoking does not permit here.
Smoking is not permit in here.
words.note: be permitted = 허용되다. allow의 격식 버전이에요.

words.ex: This app works on any device.
use: Please turn off all electronic devices.
mcq: I bought a new device for testing.
I bought a new device machine.
I bought a device equipment.
I bought a machinery device tool.
words.note: device 하나면 충분! 비슷한 말을 겹쳐 쓰지 않아요.

words.ex: It's been a long journey to this success.
use: The journey from Seoul to Paris takes 14 hours.
Learning English is a journey, not a race.
mcq: How was your journey?
How was your journey trip?
Did you journey well travel?
How did your journey travel?
words.note: journey는 긴 이동·여정. trip(짧은 여행)과 겹쳐 쓰지 않기!

words.ex: They rejected our first offer.
use: The buyer rejected the samples due to quality.
mcq: They rejected our proposal.
They rejected to our proposal.
They rejected about our proposal.
They made reject our proposal.
words.note: reject + 대상 바로 연결. refuse보다 공식적인 거절 느낌.

words.ex: Have faith in yourself.
use: I have faith in this team.
mcq: I have faith in our new product.
I have faith to our new product.
I have faith about our product.
I am faith in our product.
words.note: faith in + 대상. 비즈니스에서 in good faith(선의로)도 자주 나와요.

words.ex: There's a big gap between the two prices.
use: We need to close the gap with competitors.
There's a gap in the market for men's skincare.
mcq: There's a gap between price and quality.
There's a gap among price and quality.
There's a gap of between prices.
The gap is between to prices.
words.note: gap between A and B. 둘 사이는 between!

words.ex: Don't let emotions drive your decisions.
use: Her voice was full of emotion.
Good ads connect with customers' emotions.
mcq: He couldn't hide his emotions.
He couldn't hide his emotional.
He couldn't hide emotionally his.
His emotion was hide.
words.note: emotion(명사) vs emotional(형용사) 구분이 포인트!
